evidence: Hydatius, Chronicon: ad Brācaram extrēmam cīvitātem Gallaeciae
Graesse, Orbis Latinus s.v. Bracharaugusta: Bracharaugusta, Bragium, Bracara Augusta, Braga
terms.comment: Pliny names it the town of the Brācarī called Augusta (NH 4.112); the short Brācara is in Hydatius’s fifth-century chronicle. The long ā is that of the people’s name, Brācarī (Lewis & Short, citing the same passage of Pliny). A town takes no preposition: Brācaram Augustam (to), Brācarae Augustae (in, at), Brācarā Augustā (from).

sources: The Latin Library texts (thelatinlibrary.com), read in a local copy, for ancient passages not quoted in Lewis & Short; cited by book and section.

J. G. Th. Graesse, Orbis Latinus, edition of F. Benedict (1909), Latin–German, read in the digitization at columbia.edu (cited as Graesse, Orbis Latinus s.v.); its forms are post-classical unless Lewis & Short has them.
